title: Transition — From Language to App
summary: Building starts with a clear product description — not code.

sections.heading: Orientation — Beginning of the Lesson
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Building starts with a clear description — not code. What is the app? For whom? What is the goal?
- Why now? You have completed the 'Speaking AI' phase. Now you will describe the idea of an app — Lovable (Building Assistant) or other tools that build from your description.
- What comes after the lesson? Just 3 sentences: Idea + User + Goal. Not programming.
- You are not becoming a programmer. You are learning to describe the product — and the tool builds from your description.

sections.heading: Tension — A Strong Idea — And You Don't Know Where to Start
sections.subtitle: A Strong Idea — And You Don't Know Where to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You open Lovable or any tool and type 'Create an AI app' — and something general comes out that is not what you have in mind.
- The problem is not the tool. The problem is that you haven't specified: Who will use it? What do they want to achieve?
- The solution: 3 clear sentences before any tool. You don't need JavaScript — you need a product description.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Building Starts with a Clear Product Request
sections.subtitle: Building Starts with a Clear Product Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Any app = 3 simple layers: Interface (what the customer sees), Backstage (what works behind it), Storage (what it remembers).
- The first step is not code — but a product description: Idea + User + Goal.
- When the three are clear, Lovable understands you from the first time.
- You are learning the description — and the tool builds. This is a bridge of trust before the technical lessons.

sections.heading: Comparison — Vague Request vs Clear Product Request
sections.subtitle: Vague Request vs Clear Product Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Vague Request | Clear Product Request |
|----------|----------------|
| 'Create an AI app for restaurants' — the tool guesses everything. You will adjust 5 times and still not reach it | 'An app for a small restaurant owner — the customer writes its ingredients and the AI suggests a recipe. Goal: First recipe in 30 seconds' — this is a real building start |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Sarah wants an AI app to help shop owners write product descriptions. What is the best first step?
Write the idea of the app + the user + the goal — before opening any tool.
Open Lovable and type 'Create an AI app'.
Learn JavaScript first.

sections.heading: Mission — Write Your Product Request
sections.subtitle: Write Your Product Request
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: This is a writing task — not programming. 5–10 minutes is enough. Delivery: 1. The idea (one sentence): What does the app do?
2. The user (one sentence): Who will use it?
3. The goal (one sentence): What do they want to achieve when finished? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| The three are clear | 60% | Each line is one sentence; the user is specified (not just 'people') |
| The goal is measurable | 40% | The goal describes an outcome — not 'a beautiful app'; you can imagine when the user 'is done' |
